title: Realized volatility looks back, but it is still useful: the golf handicap reply
summary: Critics say comparing backward-looking realized volatility with forward-looking implied volatility mixes apples and oranges. The speaker agrees in part, then compares it with golf handicaps: they also look back, but you would still bet on the scratch golfer over a 12 handicap. He uses his VAY metric daily for covered calls and cash-secured puts.

steps.caption: Realized volatility is measured on past moves: it looks back.
Implied volatility is priced on the future: it looks forward.
The gap is still a useful guide, like a handicap: past form predicts future form often enough to bet on.
Realized volatility can jump. Treat the gap as one input, not a certainty.

takeaways: Realized volatility is backward-looking; implied is forward-looking.
Past volatility is still informative, like a golf handicap.
Use the implied-realized gap as part of a daily process.
caveats: VAY is the speaker's own metric; its predictive value is not verified here. Promotional link in bio.
